{{Quote|I owe the ''Outrider'' the best. She's brought me home when any other ship would have scattered me across space.|[[Dash Rendar/Legends|Dash Rendar]]|<ref name="EVV" />}}
The '''''Outrider''''' was a heavily modified [[YT-2400 light freighter/Legends|YT-2400 light freighter]] used by the brash [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] [[Dash Rendar/Legends|Dash Rendar]]. Rendar held that his ship was almost as well known as the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']].

==Design and modifications==
[[File:Outrider_schem.jpg|thumb|left|250px|''Outrider'' [[:Category:Technical drawing images|schematics]]]]

The ''Outrider'' started life as a stock [[Corellian Engineering Corporation/Legends|Corellian Engineering Corporation]] YT-2400. Like all the ships in the [[YT-series/Legends|YT-series]], the ''Outrider'' featured the trademark saucer-shaped hull, which Rendar reinforced with titanium armor and gave a dark, chrome gleam. The cockpit and main escape pod were attached to the starboard side of the saucer with two bracing arms. The docking hatch and another escape pod were on the port side.<ref name="EVV" />

One of the first modifications Dash made was to replace the original engines with three [[KonGar Ship Works|KonGar]] [[KGDefender ion engine|KGDefender]] military-grade [[Ion engine/Legends|ion engines]]<ref name="EVV" /> stolen from the advanced engineering department of the [[Imperial Academy/Legends|Imperial Academy]] on [[Corulag/Legends|Corulag]]. The factory-issue [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]] was also replaced with a modified [[SoroSuub Corporation/Legends|SoroSuub]] Griffyn/Y2TG hyperdrive, giving the ''Outrider'' a Class 0.75 hyperdrive rating.<ref name="EVV" /> The backup hyperdrive engine had a Class 10 performance. Rendar also improved the ''Outrider''{{'s}} sensors and added a countermeasure/stealth package. Though these last modifications were highly illegal, they helped him to avoid unnecessary conflicts.

When Rendar could not avoid combat, the ''Outrider'' was more than capable of holding its own. The ship was armed with a pair of [[Dymek/Legends|Dymek]] heavy [[Laser cannon/Legends|laser cannons]], mounted on dorsal and ventral turrets. The standard Corellian 1D servo mounts provided a 180-degree range of fire above and below the ship. These cannons were hand-modified by Rendar to improve both firepower and range, and could be fired from the gunnery wells or from the cockpit. The ''Outrider'' was also armed with a pair of forward-firing [[Concussion missile/Legends|concussion missile]] launchers built into the cockpit tube. Each launcher contained a magazine of three missiles.<ref name="EVV" />

The ''Outrider'' was customized to be operated by Rendar and/or [[LE-BO2D9/Legends|Leebo]]. It could carry about 75 metric tons of cargo, in addition to up to four additional passengers. When fully stocked, it could go for two standard months before needing to resupply.

==History==
<div style="float:right">[[File:Outrider-SOTETC.jpg|thumb|left|250px|''Outrider'' in action]]</div>
When asked how he acquired his ship, Rendar typically answered, "Not by clean living." The ''Outrider'' was a gift from "Uncle" [[Vanya]], a Twi'lek crime boss for whom Dash worked during the early days of his mercenary career. Vanya also provided Rendar with a [[Rodian/Legends|Rodian]] co-pilot who ended up dying within the first twenty seconds of Rendar's debut mission.

Rendar immediately began modifying the ship for smuggling duties. Most of the original modifications were done at the [[Byblos Starport Tower 214]] by Rendar and the talented [[Sullustan/Legends|Sullustan]] engineer [[Bolabo Hujaan]].

Sometime before the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin 4]], the ''Outrider'' was smuggling cargo through [[Maw Cluster/Legends|the Maw]] when it was ambushed by the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. Rendar and his navigator, [[Eaden Vrill]], were able to escape by using a hyperspace jump, but it blew out the primary and secondary hyperdrive engines. They limped to [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] on their ion engines and laid the ''Outrider'' in a berth in [[Mos Eisley/Legends|Mos Eisley]] to effect repairs. Rendar was able to hire his crew to the [[holostar]] [[Javul Charn]] to get the required money to pay for repairs.<ref name="Shadow Games">''[[Shadow Games]]''</ref>

[[File:Outrider-BMF6.png|thumb|left|250px|The ''Outrider'' orbiting Tatooine]]
Dash and Leebo were infamous in smuggling circles well before they were hired by the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] to smuggle weapons and badly needed supplies to [[Echo Base/Legends|Echo Base]] on [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]] after the evacuation of [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]]. When the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]] began, the ''Outrider'' was still berthed in Echo Base's hangar. Dash and Leebo barely escaped the base, and had to fly through the [[Hoth asteroid field/Legends|Hoth asteroid field]] in order to escape the orbiting [[Death Squadron/Legends|Death Squadron]].<ref name="Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire video game">[[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (video game)|''Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire'' video game]]</ref>

Soon afterwards, the ''Outrider'' was stationed in the [[Rebel base (Kile)|prefabricated base]] of [[Kile]]. It to accompanied the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']] in an attempt to rescue [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] from the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]], who had set down for repairs at the Imperial Enclave on the moon of [[Gall/Legends|Gall]].<ref name="novel">[[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (novel)|''Shadows of the Empire'' novel]]</ref>

The ''Outrider'' also participated in a battle to secure the Imperial freighter ''[[Suprosa]]'', which was carrying [[Death Star II plans|the plans]] for the [[Death Star II/Legends|second Death Star]].<ref name="novel" />

Rendar also piloted the ''Outrider'' during the final conflict with [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]] leader [[Prince/Legends|Prince]] [[Xizor/Legends|Xizor]] over [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]. In [[Battle over Coruscant|that battle]] it appeared that the ''Outrider'' was destroyed and Rendar and Leebo were killed, but it was a trick of timing and perspective; Rendar had decided that his time as a Rebel was over.

==Behind the scenes==
LucasArts developer and artist [[Jon Knoles]] came up with a triangular ship design<ref name="Battleships">''[[The Secrets of Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire]]'', Part 4: Battle Zones, II. Battleships</ref> that was less of a technical challenge. In retrospect, he would feel the design was too derivative of other ships of different franchises.<ref name="Twitter">{{Twitter|jonk1969|status/1290012901776924674|[[Jon Knoles]]|quote=And my early sketch for Dash Rendar's ship, The Outrider. I wasn't happy with it, as didn't look very "Star Wars" to me. More like an "Aliens" dropship.|archivedate=20230630004029}}</ref> [[Kilian Plunkett]] provided his own early concept with a unusual collapsible design.<ref name="Battleships" />

[[Industrial Light & Magic|ILM]] veteran artist [[Doug Chiang]] helped design several ships of the project, including the ''[[Virago]]'' and ''[[IG-2000/Legends|IG-2000]]''. A November [[1994]] memo by [[Allan Kausch]] proposed that the ''Outrider'' would be derivative of the ''[[Millennium Falcon/Legends|Millennium Falcon]]'', to mirror Dash's role as of a similar mold as Solo, but smaller, and not too similar. [[Sue Rostoni]] also included the guideline that it should be comparable but smaller than the ''Falcon''. Initially Chiang experimented with a pincerlike form.<ref name="Battleships" /> Knoles gave Chiang the direction that the ''Outrider'' should be "a B-Wing mated with a ''Millennium Falcon''." After just one sketch, Chiang had essentially created the final iconic version of the ship to the great satisfaction of Knoles and the team.<ref name="Forcematerial">{{WebCite|url=https://www.forcematerial.com/home/2020/5/4/jon-knoles-shadows-of-the-empire-episode-1-racer-lucasarts|archivedate=20200610171907|text=Force Material Episode LXXXVII: Jon Knoles on Shadows of the Empire, Episode I Racer and the legacy of LucasArts|date=2020-05-04|format=Podcast}}</ref><ref name="Battleships" /> Jon Knoles proceeded with the schmematics of the ''Outrider'' derived from Chiang's sketches on [[February 22]] [[1995]], in order for the video game model to be built.<ref name="Battleships" />

The final shape of the ''Outrider'' (as well as other vehicles and objects) was determined while the [[Shadows of the Empire 2|''Shadows of the Empire'' 2]] comic was under development, forcing artist Kilian Plunkett to erase his drawings and remake them with the revised design.<ref name="The Secrets of Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire">''[[The Secrets of Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire]]'', Part 5: Shadow Play, I. GATHERING OF THE TRIBES</ref>

The [[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (toy line)|toy line]] by [[Kenner Products|Hasbro/Kenner]] produced a model or the ''Outrider'' where the central port-to-starboard section of the hull could pivot like a swing-arm, and give a cross-like shape to the ship during battle.<ref>{{KennerCite|set=Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (toy line)|pack=Dash Rendar's ''Outrider''|link=soteKoutrider.asp}}</ref><ref name="Battleships" /> This feature hasn't appeared or been described in any canonical source.

Due to the increasing collaboration between LucasArts and [[Industrial Light & Magic]], the ILM department enquired about any hi-resolution models in the LucasArts archive they could possibly use for the [[The Star Wars Trilogy Special Edition|Special Edition]] releases of the original trilogy. Knoles and the rest of the ''Shadows of the Empire'' team had actually created a hi-res model of the ''Outrider'' for reference, not ever expecting it to appear in any media; when the ILM team saw the model, they liked it enough to decide to include it in a scene of [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''A New Hope'']].<ref name="Forcematerial" />
